report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of 6 of daedalus/council/session.py: dry_run_plan, _role_for, _is_local_http, default_participants, LiveCouncilRefused, live_egress_seats, and start of convene. Claims assessed; most kept, some uncheckable, no broken found.
risks: default_participants | medium | The docstring claims lanes come from council profiles, but the code derives the local lane from the resolved host, not from any profile; the claim is a documentation/behavior mismatch that could mislead about lane provenance. | Check the council profile code in another module to see if lanes are ever read; if not, the docstring is misleading.

live_egress_seats | medium | The function relies on _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS and _vendors being defined elsewhere; if the name resolution changes, the hook test could be skipped or the class check could fail open. | Inspect the definitions of _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS and _vendors in the vendors module to confirm they exist and are populated correctly.

convene | medium | The live gate checks only HTTP endpoints for trusted-lane downgrade; a trusted lane over a non-HTTP remote transport (e.g., SSH) would not be caught. | Confirm whether non-HTTP remote transports are possible; if so, the check is incomplete.

convene | low | The docstring says the refusal happens 'before the council id, before the store, before the roster is chained', but the code only shows the gate before those lines; the actual ordering depends on the rest of the function. | Read the remainder of convene to verify the ordering.

handoff.purpose: Examines dry_run_plan, _role_for, _is_local_http, default_participants, LiveCouncilRefused, live_egress_seats, and the opening of convene, verifying docstring claims against the code.

symbols.name: dry_run_plan
symbols.note: Builds an advisory plan dict without making any vendor calls; only uses pure identity properties.

symbols.name: _role_for
symbols.note: Deterministically assigns a role from the pool using (index + round_no - 1) modulo pool length.

symbols.name: VENDOR_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple of vendor keys: anthropic, openai, google, local.

symbols.name: _HTTP_HOST_RE
symbols.note: Regex to extract the host from an HTTP(S) URL.

symbols.name: _is_local_http
symbols.note: Returns True only if the endpoint matches an HTTP(S) URL and the resolved host is in _LOCAL_HOSTS.

symbols.name: default_participants
symbols.note: Builds the default roster of adapters from vendor keys, with explicit host and lane handling for the local adapter.

symbols.name: LiveCouncilRefused
symbols.note: Exception raised when a live seat is offered without live=True; deliberately not a ValueError.

symbols.name: live_egress_seats
symbols.note: Returns a tuple of seat descriptions that could reach a real vendor, fail-closed.

symbols.name: convene
symbols.note: Runs the council and returns a CouncilRecord; enforces live gate, duplicate identity check, and trusted lane adjustments.

claims.text: Exactly what :func:`convene` would do, WITHOUT calling anything. No adapter method that could reach a vendor is touched: only the identity properties (actor, independence class, lane), which are pure.
claims.why: The function only reads actor, independence_class, lane, and other pure data; it never calls adapter methods or vendor endpoints.

claims.text: True only for a loopback HTTP endpoint. ``localhost``-ish and nothing else.
claims.why: The regex matches only http/https URLs and the host must be in _LOCAL_HOSTS (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost).

claims.text: "Local" was a property of an environment variable nobody had ever set; here it is a property of the RESOLVED host, checked, not asserted.
claims.why: The function checks the resolved host from the URL, not an environment variable; it uses regex matching and a frozenset membership test.

claims.text: Lanes come from the council profiles, NOT from a default argument here: ``codex`` and ``agy`` are ``untrusted`` (allow-list tier ON) unless the operator opts in per council.
claims.why: This chunk does not show council profiles or how codex/agy lanes are set; it only shows the local adapter's lane being set explicitly based on host.

claims.text: The Ollama host is passed EXPLICITLY and ``OLLAMA_HOST`` is neither read for routing nor written -- normalising a remote Ollama into this process would retroactively falsify ``offload.py``'s ``lane="trusted"`` justification from a code path nobody edited.
claims.why: The function takes ollama_host as an explicit parameter and does not read OLLAMA_HOST; it passes host to OllamaAdapter and sets lane based on _is_local_http.

claims.text: LANE DERIVED FROM THE RESOLVED HOST, not from the provider name.
claims.why: The lane is set to 'trusted' if _is_local_http(host) else 'untrusted', independent of the provider name 'local'.

claims.text: ``OllamaAdapter`` defaults to ``lane="trusted"`` whatever host it is given, and "trusted" means the tier-2 allow-list is OFF and ``withheld`` is empty -- correct ONLY while no bytes leave the machine.
claims.why: The default lane of OllamaAdapter is not visible in this chunk; the comment claims it defaults to trusted, but that is defined in the vendors module.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT a ``ValueError``: every other refusal in :func:`convene` is a malformed-roster complaint, and "you were about to spend money" must be catchable on its own.
claims.why: LiveCouncilRefused subclasses RuntimeError, not ValueError, and the code raises it for live seats, distinct from ValueError for other roster issues.

claims.text: Name every seat that could actually reach a vendor.  FAIL-CLOSED.
claims.why: The function counts a seat as live unless it is not a shipped class, its _dispatch is overridden, or its hooks are substituted; otherwise it is live.

claims.text: The question is not "is this class from :mod:`vendors`" -- it is "if ``ask()`` runs, does SHIPPED transport code execute".
claims.why: The function checks whether the adapter is an instance of shipped classes and whether _dispatch is defined in _vendors, and whether hooks are in _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS.

claims.text: A seat is therefore counted as LIVE unless one of these is demonstrably true: it is not one of the shipped concrete adapters at all; its ``_dispatch`` is defined OUTSIDE :mod:`daedalus.council.vendors`; its ``runner`` / ``chat`` hook is not one of :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS`.
claims.why: The code checks each condition: not isinstance of shipped_classes, dispatch module != _vendors.__name__, and hook not in _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS; otherwise appends to live.

claims.text: If :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS` ever resolves empty (vendors renamed something), the hook test is SKIPPED rather than trivially satisfied, so the failure lands on the safe side.
claims.why: The code wraps the hook check in `if _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS:` so if it is empty, the check is skipped, and the seat is still counted live (fail-closed).

claims.text: ``participants`` are :class:`vendors.CouncilAdapter` instances -- read-only, tool-less, spawned outside the repo.  Every one of them is REQUESTED, and every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn per round even when it is missing: skipping an unavailable vendor would let a two-vendor council render identically to a four-vendor one.
claims.why: This chunk does not show the chaining logic that would produce one turn per round; it only shows the start of convene.

claims.text: ``trusted_vendors`` is the OPERATOR OPT-IN that lifts a vendor off the untrusted allow-list for this council only.  It is recorded per participant, because deciding OpenAI or Google is trusted with this repo's IP is a policy decision and a default argument must not make it.
claims.why: The code sets adapter.lane = 'trusted' for vendors in trusted_vendors, and trusted_vendors defaults to () so no vendor is trusted by default.

claims.text: ``live`` is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False.  Any seat that still carries a shipped vendor transport (:func:`live_egress_seats`) raises :class:`LiveCouncilRefused` here -- before the council id, before the store, before the roster is chained, before one byte is dispatched.
claims.why: The code checks `if not live:` and calls live_egress_seats; if seats are found, it raises LiveCouncilRefused before generating council_id or store path.

claims.text: Offline adapters (fakes, injected runners) are unaffected, so the replay harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: live_egress_seats only counts seats with shipped transports; fakes or injected runners would be filtered out, so they would not trigger the refusal.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the live-wire gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach `sorted()` empty -- a council of nobody, chained as if it were real.
claims.why: The code converts participants to a tuple immediately, ensuring it is not a one-shot iterator before the gate and sorted() calls.

claims.text: Two seats with one identity: local qwen2.5-coder:7b and BENCH qwen2.5-coder:7b are the same weights on two sockets and would land as one indistinguishable pair of turns. Refuse loudly rather than let the transcript claim two voices it cannot tell apart.
claims.why: The code checks for duplicate actor identities and raises ValueError if found, refusing to proceed.

claims.text: A trusted lane over an HTTP endpoint on ANOTHER MACHINE turns the tier-2 allow-list off and reports ``withheld=[]`` while full repo source crosses the tailnet. That is precisely the justification ``offload.py:193-197`` rests on ("no bytes leave the machine"), borrowed by a host it was never written for. Fail closed and make ...
claims.why: The code checks if adapter.lane == 'trusted' and endpoint is remote HTTP, then presumably downgrades to untrusted (the rest of the logic is truncated but the condition is present).

observations.what: The default_participants docstring claims lanes come from council profiles, but the code only sets the local adapter's lane explicitly based on host; the claim may be misleading about the source of lanes for other adapters.
live_egress_seats relies on _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS and _vendors being defined elsewhere; if they are not populated correctly, the hook test could be skipped or the class check could fail open.
The trusted-lane downgrade in convene only checks HTTP endpoints via _HTTP_HOST_RE; non-HTTP remote transports (e.g., SSH) would not be caught.
The docstring for convene claims the live refusal happens before council id and store, but the code only shows the gate before those lines; the rest of the function is not in this chunk.
